description: MCP-style sync tool catalog for FRIDAY LLM tool selection. Async specs live in executor/tools/<category>.py; sync metadata here; handlers in executor/tool_handlers.py; dispatch in executor/tools_registry.py.

safety_levels.low: Read-only, informational, or easily reversible actions.
safety_levels.medium: UI/input changes, messaging, or automation that affects open applications.
safety_levels.high: Destructive or hard-to-reverse system actions (shutdown, sleep, privileged commands).

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Launch or focus a Windows application by name or alias. Resolves common names (chrome, notepad, calculator, vscode, spotify, discord, whatsapp, terminal, settings). Does not perform in-app UI steps after launch.

app.description: Application name or alias to launch (e.g. chrome, notepad, spotify).

tools.when_to_use: User wants to open or switch to an application without further automation inside it.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to send a WhatsApp message (use send_whatsapp) or click/type inside an app (use web_agent or type_text).

tools.name: send_whatsapp_message
tools.description: Send a WhatsApp message to a named contact. Opens WhatsApp Desktop, searches the contact, types the message, and sends it. Requires the contact name as saved in WhatsApp.

contact.description: Contact name as it appears in WhatsApp.

tools.when_to_use: User explicitly asks to message someone on WhatsApp with message content.
tools.when_not_to_use: User only wants WhatsApp opened (use open_app with app=whatsapp).

examples.user: send sathish a message on whatsapp saying hi

tools.name: play_music
tools.description: Play a song on Spotify Web, YouTube, or YouTube Music. Infer platform from phrases like 'on spotify', 'on youtube', or 'on youtube music'. If the user says only 'play music' with no song, default to AC/DC Back in Black on Spotify Web (browser, not desktop app).

song.description: Song title or artist + title to play.

tools.when_to_use: User wants to start playback of a specific song or resume music on a named streaming service.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants next/previous/pause only (use media controls via graph) or a browser search without playback.

tools.name: play_youtube_music
tools.description: Play a song specifically on YouTube Music (music.youtube.com). Use when the user names YouTube Music explicitly, not generic YouTube video playback.

song.description: Song to search and play on YouTube Music.

tools.when_to_use: User explicitly mentions YouTube Music.
tools.when_not_to_use: User mentions Spotify or plain YouTube (use play_music or play_youtube).

tools.name: play_spotify_music
tools.description: Play a song on Spotify Web. Narrower than play_music — use when the user names Spotify without mentioning other platforms.

song.description: Song to search and play on Spotify.

tools.when_to_use: User explicitly wants Spotify playback.
tools.when_not_to_use: User also specifies youtube or youtube music (use play_music with platform).

tools.name: play_youtube
tools.description: Play a video or song on YouTube (youtube.com), not YouTube Music. Opens YouTube and searches for the requested title.

song.description: Video or song title to search on YouTube.

tools.when_to_use: User wants YouTube video playback specifically.
tools.when_not_to_use: User says YouTube Music (use play_youtube_music).

examples.user: play never gonna give you up on youtube

tools.name: search_browser
tools.description: Open the default browser and run a Google search. Search-only: does not click results, scroll pages, or read article content.

query.description: Search query to submit to Google.

tools.when_to_use: User wants search results opened in the browser with no follow-up navigation.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to open/read/scroll an article (use search_and_browse) or a spoken answer (use smart_search).

tools.name: search_and_browse
tools.description: Compound automation: open Chrome, Google-search a query, click the first result, and scroll the page. Use when the user wants search plus navigation in one request.

query.description: Specific search query. Rewrite vague terms like 'any article' into a concrete topic.

scroll.description: Whether to scroll after opening the first result. Defaults to true.

tools.when_to_use: User asks to search, open a result, and/or scroll in a single utterance.
tools.when_not_to_use: User only wants tabs opened with search results (use search_browser) or a summarized answer (use smart_search).

examples.user: search for AI news and scroll

tools.name: read_headlines
tools.description: Fetch and speak the top news headlines (typically three) from Google News for a topic. Returns spoken briefing text, not browser navigation.

query.description: News topic or 'latest news'. Defaults to general headlines.

tools.when_to_use: User wants a spoken news headline briefing.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to browse full articles in the browser (use search_and_browse).

tools.name: smart_search
tools.description: Answer factual questions with tiered web lookup: DuckDuckGo API, DuckDuckGo HTML scrape, then LLM fallback. Returns a concise answer suitable for speech — no browser UI automation.

query.description: Question or topic to research and summarize.

tools.when_to_use: User asks a factual question and wants a direct spoken answer.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants browser navigation, clicking, or scrolling (use search_browser, search_and_browse, or web_agent).

tools.name: mouse_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the active window or page up or down by a number of wheel ticks. Does not use vision or element targeting.

amount.description: Number of scroll steps. Defaults to 3.

tools.when_to_use: User wants simple page or window scrolling.
tools.when_not_to_use: User needs to find and click a named on-screen element (use web_agent).

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current screen and save a PNG image to the user's Desktop folder.
tools.when_to_use: User wants a saved screenshot file on Desktop.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants OCR or text extraction from the screen (use screen_read in the graph pipeline).

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type literal text at the currently focused input or cursor. Subject to window-context preflight checks when an app is specified.

text.description: Exact text to type into the focused field.

interval.description: Optional delay between keystrokes in seconds.

app.description: Optional target app name for window-context preflight checks.

tools.when_to_use: User provides exact text to enter in the focused application.
tools.when_not_to_use: User describes clicking a named button or multi-step form workflows (use web_agent).

tools.name: click_at
tools.description: Click at explicit screen pixel coordinates. Only valid when the user supplies numeric x and y values — never infer coordinates from element names.
tools.when_to_use: User gives exact pixel coordinates for a click.
tools.when_not_to_use: User refers to a named UI element like 'login button' (use web_agent).

tools.name: browser_agent
tools.description: DOM-based browser automation with human-like Puppeteer interaction. Search, open sites, play music, and control media via structured page state + LangChain agent (no vision).
tools.when_to_use: User wants in-browser automation: search, navigate, music, media controls.
tools.when_not_to_use: Native desktop apps like WhatsApp (use send_whatsapp) or spoken answers only (use smart_search).

examples.user: search for AI news and open the first article

params.task: search for AI news and open the first article

tools.name: web_agent
tools.description: Deprecated alias for browser_agent. DOM-based browser automation (no vision).

task.description: Full natural-language description of the automation task to perform.

query.description: Alias for task when phrased as a query.

tools.when_to_use: User needs UI automation by element name, vision, or multi-step workflows.
tools.when_not_to_use: User provides exact coordinates (use click_at) or only wants a Google search tab (use search_browser).

tools.name: move_mouse
tools.description: Move the mouse cursor visibly to exact screen coordinates supplied by the user. Does not click.
tools.when_to_use: User supplies explicit coordinates to reposition the mouse.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to click a named element (use web_agent).

tools.name: hotkey
tools.description: Press a keyboard shortcut such as ctrl+c, alt+tab, or win+d. Accepts keys joined by + in a single string.
tools.when_to_use: User requests a specific keyboard shortcut.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to type readable text (use type_text).

tools.name: volume_control
tools.description: Change system volume: mute, unmute, increase, or decrease by a number of steps.

amount.description: Steps for up/down actions. Defaults to 5.

tools.when_to_use: User wants to change or mute system audio levels.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants media track skip/pause (use graph media tools).

tools.name: system_command
tools.description: Run a whitelisted diagnostic Windows command: taskmgr, systeminfo, ipconfig, hostname, whoami, ver, battery report, or similar. Arbitrary shell commands are rejected.

command.description: Allowed command prefix (e.g. taskmgr, systeminfo, ipconfig).

tools.when_to_use: User requests diagnostic or system information via an approved command.
tools.when_not_to_use: User requests shutdown, restart, or lock (use graph system tools) or unrestricted shell access.

tools.name: cancel_task
tools.description: Cancel or stop running background tasks managed by FRIDAY's task manager. Use task_type 'all' to stop every active task.

task_type.description: Task type to cancel, or 'all' to stop every active background task.

tools.when_to_use: User wants to interrupt FRIDAY background work or long-running tasks.
tools.when_not_to_use: User wants to close a desktop application window (use window_close in the graph pipeline).

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Conversational pass-through when no tool execution is required. Use for greetings, acknowledgements, or delivering a final spoken answer after data has been gathered.

response.description: Optional assistant response text when handled inline.

tools.when_to_use: Greetings, small talk, or summarizing results when no action tool applies.
tools.when_not_to_use: User requests any concrete system, UI, or web action — select a specific tool instead.
